title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
metadata_mismatch: none in title/authors; PDF abstract wording slightly differs from metadata abstract (PDF calls it a 'working note' from a 'three day sprint')
why_wsp: Replication of Takehi et al.: GPT-6 Astra and other LLMs write MinAtar/MNIST network weights in one tool-free reply, read raw weights to name games, decompile written networks into Python, and audit poisoned LMs/adapters from plain-text weights.
domain: MinAtar games, MNIST digits, small diffusion models, poisoned Olmo 3 190M LMs, Qwen3.5-0.8B adapters
editor: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; earlier Claude Opus 4.5/5, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.6 Sol; open-weight Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Kimi-K3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3.8-27B
target: small MLPs (Breakout network '20,486 weight'), MNIST MLP (784-32-32-10), Olmo 3 190M models, Qwen3.5-0.8B adapters
interface: direct values (single reply, no tools) for writing; plain-text weight files with file read/write but no Python for auditing; Python analysis allowed for decompilation
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Astra's Breakout network: 'only 815 of the 20,486 are non-zero, and only 6 of the 32 first-layer units are used at all' (Sec. 2.1)

headline_results.quote: Across three runs on Breakout, Astra’s networks scored 514, 550 and 307, in line with the 517 score reported in the MIT results.

headline_results.claim: Novel game variants rule out recall
headline_results.quote: the networks it wrote for these custom variations averaged 515 on both
Both programs choose the same move as the written network in 100% of the 49,189 game states we tested

headline_results.claim: MNIST written network below template baseline
headline_results.quote: Astra’s networks scored 49.6% on average over three runs (55.7, 47.2 and 46.0%).

headline_results.claim: Reading: game identification and shuffled control
headline_results.quote: Astra and Opus 5.5 named the game every time (12 of 12 over three runs each).
Astra picked out the model poisoned during training in all 10 runs.

headline_results.claim: Auditing: malicious adapter detection, no trigger found
headline_results.quote: Astra, on the other hand, was able to correctly guess 23 of 32 arrangements

headline_results.claim: Opus 5.5 often fails to emit weights
headline_results.quote: it often spends its whole output budget thinking and never writes the weights (5 of 9 runs)

cost.quote: Opus 5.5 finished in about six minutes and 37,000 output tokens, Astra in about four minutes and 9,000 tokens.
4 of 32 hitting the 300-turn limit (around 150k output tokens and 10M input tokens)

baselines_and_controls: original post's PPO baselines (noted as probably under-tuned); Python-program versions of same policy; MNIST trained net (96.7%) and template classifier (82.0%); weight-shuffle control for reading; novel/modified games (swapped, upside-down Breakout, rotated MNIST); networks trained by authors on new games; earlier-generation and open-weight models
runs_and_variance: 'Most results come from one to five runs per model and task (a single run for the Python programs), and scores vary between runs.' (Sec. 7); e.g. Breakout 514/550/307
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning/quantization); networks written for standard Breakout score 0.5 and 0.0 on modified variants
verification: none formal; decompiled programs checked against network on 49,189 states
memorization_vs_reasoning: Novel Breakout variants and rotated MNIST show networks are written for the stated input, not recalled; reading is mostly input-layer layout (heatmaps), with mechanics often missed and familiar game names substituted ('Frogger'); auditing relied on heuristics (untrained special-token embeddings) and never found triggers.
limitations_stated: Three-day sprint; only some experiments replicated; code written by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra and not independently reviewed; 1-5 runs; API failures; reasoning-effort settings not comparable; proprietary models may change; small networks and one fuzzy task; post's networks now public; decompilation restrictions were instructions not enforced.
notes_for_survey: Independent replication that confirms B2 writing on MinAtar and frames written networks as compiled programs (exact decompilation), with an MNIST negative control. Reading results are attributed largely to input-layer layout. Plain-text-weight auditing detects which model is poisoned in easy cases but never recovers the trigger or behaviour.
